results.title: Qwertykeys is rated "Poor" with 2.5 / 5 on Trustpilot
results.content:
## Great Products, But Customer Support Needs Improvement
I really love the quality of the keyboards and accessories from QuertyKeys — the design, feel, and performance of the products are excellent and honestly stand out in this price range. The build quality is solid, and the overall experience of using the gear has been great.  
  
However, I did have a frustrating experience with customer support. When I reached out with questions, the responses felt unfriendly and not very helpful, which was disappointing. I’d love to see improvements here because the products deserve support that’s just as good. [...] but after a few times, it makes more sense or I just asked people on Discord where to find things. Another important mention, if you're looking for a mechanical keyboard, this company stocks their keyboard parts for yearssss. You can buy replacement or more parts later on unlike most other companies in this hobby that basically if your keyboard breaks, you're done for cause no replacement parts available. So yeah. Qwertykeys keyboards tick all the right boxes for me. I'm happy to recommend them to anyone. [...] Qwerty Keys sent me the wrong item and when I contacted customer support, they offered me $30 when the keyboard I ordered was $175 value. What a slap in the face. Mind you, this was THEIR mistake. I politely declined and asked for the item I originally ordered or a different keyboard of equal or lesser value. They instead offered me $50, still less than 1/3 the value of the item I originally ordered. Again, I politely declined. We ended up settling on a refund AND I have to send them back the wrong item I received. Worst experience ever with a greedy company. At the end of the day, they could have just sent me the item I ordered, but no. @yoann\_berno3 I realized that it's hard to vibe code these mini games, there's a lot of work involved in capturing the right "feel." I think it was refactored twice at least, first versions of mechanic were so boring. I had a hard time trying to work on other projects while working on these games. Even though Claude is handling the coding, unit tests don't really capture how fun, hard, or frustrating the game is, so I feel I need to be actively involved in working on it. In other words, it was manually tuned a lot.

Diego Dotta

@yoann\_berno3 and I still feel like I could spend more time tweaking it, adding more country layouts and other details.

Ziang Yang [...] ### Top forum threads

What do you think? …

Diego Dotta

This is a small game sponsored by Smart Keys (a smart keyboard for iOS and MacOS) that I've been wanting to build for a long time, so here it is.

I think the difficulty is a little off and I can't see it straight anymore, I've played this thing roughly four thousand times, so everything feels "normal" to me now, which is exactly the problem.  
  
My hunch: Level 1 might be too gentle, and the jump right after it too mean. But I'd rather hear it from you. If you bounce off a level, breeze through one, or hit the wall at a specific spot, tell me where in the comments. I read every single one and I'll be tweaking based on what you say. 🙏  
  
If you pass level 8, congratulations, you are a Tetris master. I mean QWERTYS beast :p.
